notes: Two protected areas sampled in different years, shipped as one table with cluster_id = area. Camera-relative day occasions, no dates. Paper paywalled; abstract used.

description: Camera-trap detections of tayra, puma and free-ranging dogs at 57 sites around Furnas do Bom Jesus State Park, Brazil, 2017, nine 12-day occasions.
reference: Bianchi, R. et al. (2021). Tayra (Eira barbara) landscape use as a function of cover types, forest protection, and the presence of puma and free-ranging dogs. Biotropica.
notes: Multi-species occupancy (three species).

description: Robust-design camera-trap capture histories of 307 tigers in Corbett National Park, India, 2010-2015: six annual primaries of 42 trap-nights, with sex and sampling block per tiger.
reference: Bisht, S., Banerjee, S., Qureshi, Q., & Jhala, Y. (2019). Demography of a high-density tiger population and its implications for tiger recovery. Journal of Applied Ecology.
notes: From the MARK .inp; 42 nights per primary from the paper (s. 2.4). Deposit's per-year counts differ from the paper's Table 2. IUCN EN, no coordinates. Dryad version zip.

description: Daily detection/non-detection of the Alpine mountain hare at 46 camera-trap stations (1,227-2,740 m) in the Mont-Blanc massif, France, September 2017 to June 2022, binned into 20 meteorological seasons, with surveyed camera-days from setup dates minus deposited downtime windows, station coordinates, elevation, slope, aspect, habitat and six vegetation-cover classes.
reference: Bison, M., Yoccoz, N. G., Carlson, B. Z., Bayle, A., & Delestrade, A. (2024). Camera traps reveal seasonal variation in activity and occupancy of the Alpine mountain hare Lepus timidus varronis. Wildlife Biology, 2024(4), e01186.
notes: Record-table source (contact days) plus a camera table with setup dates and downtime windows but no end dates: survey set inferred to 2022-06-30 (abstract). Season binning is the processor's; the paper's occasion and season definitions were not reachable. Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Weekly counts of independent grey wolf and brown bear camera-trap detections at 229 deployments (2009-2023) in and around Sarikamis-Allahuekber Mountains National Park, northeastern Turkiye, up to 104 seven-day occasions per deployment, with camera, topographic, land-cover, distance and human-activity covariates.
reference: Blount, J. D., Green, A. M., Chynoweth, M., Coban, E., Kusak, J. & Sekercioglu, C. H. (2025). Combining N-mixture and occupancy analysis offers a more complete picture of carnivore habitat use in Northeastern Turkiye. PLOS One 20(5), e0320768.
notes: Matrices have no row ids; aligned to the covariate sheet by row order (229 each). 13 deployments have no surveyed week. Lynx counts not alignable (215 x 472); lynx 0/1 in blount_2025_neturkiye_lynx_occ.

description: Eurasian lynx detection / non-detection per seven-day occasion at 229 camera deployments (2009-2023) in and around Sarikamis-Allahuekber Mountains National Park, northeastern Turkiye, with camera, topographic, land-cover, distance and human-activity covariates; sibling of the wolf and bear count table.
reference: Blount, J. D., Green, A. M., Chynoweth, M., Coban, E., Kusak, J. & Sekercioglu, C. H. (2025). Combining N-mixture and occupancy analysis offers a more complete picture of carnivore habitat use in Northeastern Turkiye. PLOS One 20(5), e0320768.
notes: 0/1 only: the lynx count matrix (215 x 472, no ids) cannot be aligned to the deployments. Same survey set as blount_2025_neturkiye_carniv_count.

description: Bumble bee counts (females, males, queens) for 15 species and species-group classes, including the endangered rusty patched bumble bee, from five one-hour active searches at 25 sites across Minnesota, June-September 2021, with survey weather, bloom and honey bee covariates and site land use; coordinates coarsened to 0.1 degree.
reference: Boone, M. (2023). 2021 Minnesota bumble bee survey data. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.0p2ngf264
notes: Taxa are identification classes as recorded, two of them species aggregates. Coordinates coarsened and site ids replaced for B. affinis; boone_2023_minnesota_bombus_exact_count has the other classes at published precision.

description: Bumble bee counts (females, males, queens) for 14 species and species-group classes (all but the endangered rusty patched bumble bee) from five one-hour active searches at 25 sites across Minnesota, June-September 2021, with survey weather, bloom and honey bee covariates and site land use; coordinates as published.
reference: Boone, M. (2023). 2021 Minnesota bumble bee survey data. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.0p2ngf264
notes: E7.3 sibling of boone_2023_minnesota_bombus_count without B. affinis; coordinates and site names as published.

description: Detection and time to first detection (seconds, censored at 8 min) of 17 grassland plant species by two independent observers in 44 quadrats in the Swiss Alps, August 2011.
reference: Bornand, C. N., Kéry, M., Bueche, L. & Fischer, M. (2014). Hide and seek in vegetation: time-to-detection is an efficient design for estimating detectability and occurrence. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 5, 433-442. https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12171
notes: Species names from the paper's Table 1 (PDF supplied by Ben); read from batch 35's cache.

description: Per-visit territory-mapping counts of Great Tit and Eurasian Blue Tit at 24 forest subsites in Switzerland, 2014-2015, as interpreted by each of three territory editors (occasion = visit x editor).
reference: Bötsch, Y., Jenni, L., & Kéry, M. (2020). Field evaluation of abundance estimates under binomial and multinomial N-mixture models. Ibis, 162. https://doi.org/10.1111/ibi.12802
notes: Territory editors as observers (ruling 2026-11-06): one table, occasion = visit x editor, closure dependent; per-territory histories not shipped.

description: Pitfall-trap presence / absence of 115 beetle taxa in five fortnightly collections at 60 farmland woodlands of known age (England and Scotland, 2013-2014), with trap numbers, woodland age, area, structure and landscape history.

description: Bird presence / absence (54 species) on up to three repeat surveys at 125 farmland woodlands of known age in England and Scotland (2015, 2017), with surveyor, date, woodland age, area, structure and landscape history.
reference: Bradfer-Lawrence, T., Dobson, A., Finch, T., et al. (2025). Data and code for "Spillovers and legacies of land management on temperate woodland biodiversity". Zenodo.
notes: 47 surveys not carried out have no rows. Siblings: _beetle_comm, _mammal_comm, _plant_comm.

description: Small-mammal live-trap presence / absence (four species) on four trap days at 100 farmland woodlands of known age in England and Scotland (2013-2014), with woodland age, area, structure and landscape history.
reference: Bradfer-Lawrence, T., Dobson, A., Finch, T., et al. (2025). Data and code for "Spillovers and legacies of land management on temperate woodland biodiversity". Zenodo.
notes: Complete matrix. Siblings: _beetle_comm, _bird_comm, _plant_comm.

description: Single-survey presence / absence of 200 vascular plant species at 129 farmland woodlands of known age in England and Scotland, with woodland age, area, structure and landscape history (no repeat visits).
reference: Bradfer-Lawrence, T., Dobson, A., Finch, T., et al. (2025). Data and code for "Spillovers and legacies of land management on temperate woodland biodiversity". Zenodo.
notes: Single visit per site (n_occasions = 1): detection not estimable from this table. Survey dates not deposited. Siblings: _beetle_comm, _bird_comm, _mammal_comm.

description: Camera-trap detection/non-detection of the rusty-margined guan at 205 sites in southeastern Brazil, six occasions, with landscape covariates.
reference: Braga, P. R. et al. (2024). Anthropogenic landscape features affect the ground habitat use of Penelope superciliaris (Cracidae). Biotropica.
notes: Single-species occupancy.

description: Counts of palila on six-minute point counts at 455 stations around Mauna Kea, Hawaii, repeated one to four times each year, 1998-2018, with observer, detection type and weather.
reference: Brinck, K.W., Genz, A.S., and Camp, R.J. (2022). Mauna Kea Palila point count data from annual surveys 1998-2018 (ver. 2.0, January 2022). U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Count per station visit; per-bird distances not shipped.

description: Search-encounter spatial capture-recapture of cheetahs in the Maasai Mara, Kenya: animal x 1-km search pixel x day over eight 90-day sessions in and out of the wildebeest migration, 2015-2018, with km driven per pixel-day; session-scoped ids; pixel coordinates centred (VU taxon).
reference: Broekhuis, F., Elliot, N. B., Keiwua, K., Koinet, K., Macdonald, D. W., Mogensen, N., Thuo, D., & Gopalaswamy, A. M. (2021). Resource pulses influence the spatio-temporal dynamics of a large carnivore population. Ecography, 44(3), 358-369.
original_license: CC0 1.0 (Dryad; ReadMe asks re-users to contact the authors)
notes: Search-encounter SCR; effort table = pixel-day operation matrix with log km driven. IUCN VU; coordinates centred.

description: Adult monarch counts on IMMP transects, three surveys per summer at 60 Wisconsin grassland sites in 2018 and 2019 (352 surveys), with nectar-species richness and milkweed density per survey, site coordinates and patch/landscape metrics.
reference: Bruce, A.S., Thogmartin, W.E., Trosen, C., Oberhauser, K., & Gratton, C. (2022). Landscape- and local-level variables affect monarchs in Midwest grasslands. Landscape Ecology, 37, 93-108.
notes: Survey dates not deposited. Egg/larva per-stem ratios not shipped.

description: Feral cat detection per 5-day occasion at 90 paired road and forest camera-trap sites across six study areas of the Australian Wet Tropics, 2019-2020, with effort and habitat covariates.
reference: Bruce, T., Williams, S. E., Amin, R., L'Hotellier, F., & Hirsch, B. T. (2022). Laying low: Rugged lowland rainforest preferred by feral cats in the Australian Wet Tropics. Ecology and Evolution, 12, e9105.
notes: NA cells (< 3 active days) not surveyed; effort scaled as deposited; no coordinates.

description: Nine-visit-per-season counts of 28 focal grassland bird species within 100 m of on-, near- and off-road stops in North Dakota (2015) and Montana (2017-2018), with observers, stop habitat and count conditions; stop locators replaced by codes.
reference: Buhl, T.K., and Shaffer, T.L. (2023). Investigating Detection and Roadside Bias in Surveys of Grassland Birds in the Northern Great Plains, ND 2015, MT 2017-2018. U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Whole table with stop and route codes; PLSS ids in the _exact sibling.

description: Nine-visit-per-season counts of 26 focal grassland bird species within 100 m of on-, near- and off-road stops in North Dakota (2015) and Montana (2017-2018), with observers, stop habitat and count conditions; IUCN-threatened species omitted, PLSS stop ids kept.
reference: Buhl, T.K., and Shaffer, T.L. (2023). Investigating Detection and Roadside Bias in Surveys of Grassland Birds in the Northern Great Plains, ND 2015, MT 2017-2018. U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: E7.3 sibling of buhl_2023_ndmt_grassbirds_count without the flagged species.

description: Camera-trap detection / non-detection of fishers at 64 sites x 64 sampling occasions, Alberta, 2016; the unmarked data set paired with the genetic SCR table burgar_2018_alberta_fisher_scr.
reference: Burgar, J. M., Stewart, F. E. C., Volpe, J. P., Fisher, J. T., & Burton, A. C. (2018). Estimating density for species conservation: Comparing camera trap spatial count models to genetic spatial capture-recapture models. Global Ecology and Conservation, 15, e00411.
notes: Single-species camera detections, complete 64 x 64 matrix. No coordinates (site numbering not keyed to the TDF). Occasion length only in the paywalled-to-agents paper.

description: Genetic spatial capture-recapture detections of 24 fishers at 64 hair-snag sites over 4 occasions in Alberta, 2016 (one row per fisher x site x occasion), with UTM site coordinates in __traps.
reference: Burgar, J. M., Stewart, F. E. C., Volpe, J. P., Fisher, J. T., & Burton, A. C. (2018). Estimating density for species conservation: Comparing camera trap spatial count models to genetic spatial capture-recapture models. Global Ecology and Conservation, 15, e00411.
notes: Closed-population genetic SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps. Survey set = TDF usage (all sites, all occasions). Sibling camera table burgar_2018_alberta_fisher_count not joinable (different site numbering). Below floor (24 individuals).

description: Camera-trap detection/non-detection of five mammals at 141 burned and unburned shrub-steppe sites in eastern Washington (four cameras per site, 2021-2024), with fire and vegetation covariates.
reference: Burgstahler, K., Shipley, L., Stift, A., Woodley, S., & Thornton, D. (2026). Effects of wildfire on the distribution of mammals and birds in a working shrub-steppe landscape. Ecosphere.
notes: Spatial-replicate occupancy from the analysis-ready histories; single-visit bird counts not built.

description: Track-group counts of nine target taxa (Iberian lynx, red fox, badger, mongoose, genet, otter, cats, hedgehog, dog) on 12 permanent sand transects in Doñana National Park, Spain, 2007-2022, about three runs a year.
reference: Carro F, Román I, Laffite Alaminos R, Paz D, Ceballos O, Chico A, Torrijo-Salesa M, Díaz-Delgado R, Bustamante J, Márquez-Ferrando R (2023). Long-term monitoring of the relative density of [taxon] with track counts in Doñana National Park 2007-2022. Estación Biológica de Doñana (CSIC). Sampling event datasets (nine, one per taxon): 10.15470/yvoou1, 10.15470/xavass, 10.15470/oaffix, 10.15470/2us9py, 10.15470/zmqncw, 10.15470/pjpxhp, 10.15470/up1q9h, 10.15470/4pcvqq, 10.15470/p09dsf
notes: Nine GBIF Spain IPT DwC-As (icts-rbd-*tracks_20230915), one per taxon, joined on their shared event set. Transect positions coarsened to 0.1 degree (lynx).

description: Calling index (0 not heard to 3 full chorus) of 26 frog and toad species and one genus-level treefrog group at the 10 stops of 54 Louisiana Amphibian Monitoring Program roadside routes, three seasonal runs a year, 1997-2017.
reference: Carter, J., Johnson, D., Boundy, J., & Vermillion, W. (2021). The Louisiana Amphibian Monitoring Program from 1997 to 2017: Results, analyses, and lessons learned. PLOS ONE, 16(9), e0257869.
original_license: US public domain (USGS data release; use constraints none)
notes: Ordinal calling index (NAAMP protocol). Unit = route stop, cluster_id = route. No coordinates in the release. Date fields shipped as month/day only (year of the December 1997 rows ambiguous).

description: Annual capture histories of 11,919 yellow-bellied toads in four French populations (two in harvested woodland, two riverine), 2000-2014, with birth year where known.
reference: Cayuela, H., Lemaitre, J.-F., Bonnaire, E., Pichenot, J., & Schmidt, B. R. (2020). Population position along the fast-slow life-history continuum predicts intraspecific variation in actuarial senescence. Journal of Animal Ecology, 89.
notes: Dryad version zip; four sheets stacked with population as cluster_id; rows start at birth year where it is later than the study start.

description: Annual capture histories of 1,553 marked diamondback terrapins (Malaclemys terrapin) on the Kiawah River, South Carolina, across 28 sampling years 1983-2012, pooled from 3,376 seine, net, hand and crab-pot captures; sex, first site, captures per year and crab-pot captures per year.
reference: Cecala, K. (2026). Long-term diamondback terrapin capture-recapture data from Kiawah Island, South Carolina (1983-2012). Dryad.
notes: Survey years inferred from capture records (2000-2001 have none). Radio relocations and unmarked animals excluded. IUCN VU species; no coordinates in source.

description: Aural detection/non-detection of the invasive Japanese burrowing cricket at 49 point-count sites in central Kentucky, three counts per site between 19 September and 5 November 2024, with the temperature, barometric pressure, wind speed, minutes since sunset and date of every count.
reference: Cecconi, S. V., Notarianni, N., & McNeil, D. J. (2025). Assessing factors associated with detection probability of the Japanese burrowing cricket (Velarifictorus micado) on point count surveys. Journal of Applied Entomology, 150(2), 200-206.
notes: Insect single-season occupancy from aural point counts. Invasive species; no coordinates deposited; date rebuilt from the ordinal day and the year in the Dryad abstract.

description: Multi-state closed robust design capture histories of 209 photo-identified Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops aduncus) at three sites in Perth metropolitan waters, Western Australia: 16 seasonal primary periods (June 2011 to May 2015) x 3-6 secondary occasions; y is the site of capture (0 not captured, 1 estuary, 2 embayment, 3 open coast). The Program MARK input for Chabanne et al. (2017) Scenario 1.
reference: Chabanne, D.B.H., Pollock, K.H., Finn, H., Bejder, L. & Gimenez, O. (2017). Applying the multistate capture-recapture robust design to characterize metapopulation structure. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 8(11), 1547-1557.
notes: Season layout of the 75 unlabelled MARK columns inferred against the thesis effort table (76 completed occasions); summer 2011-12 carries 4 columns. 2-state (Scenario 2) file not shipped. One duplicated id relabelled.

description: Automated acoustic detection counts of the pig frog at 60 sites x 8 occasions, with validated true / false positives.
reference: Chambert, T. et al. (2018). A new framework for analysing automated acoustic species detection data. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9(3), 560-570.
notes: Counts of classifier detections with false-positive validation.

description: Field-identified detections of the endangered Shenandoah salamander and the red-backed salamander at 131 sites in Shenandoah National Park, 2011-2014 (2-5 surveys per year), with the joint field state and the DNA-confirmed identity where available: the worked example for two-species occupancy with misidentification.
reference: Chambert, T., Grant, E. H. C., Miller, D. A. W., Nichols, J. D., Mulder, K. P., & Brand, A. B. (2018). Two-species occupancy modelling accounting for species misidentification and non-detection. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9(6), 1468-1477.
notes: First species-misidentification table: joint field state in y_raw, DNA confirmation in obs_dna_state. No coordinates deposited.

description: Automated acoustic detection counts of the green treefrog at 60 sites x 6 occasions, with validated true / false positives.
reference: Chambert, T. et al. (2018). A new framework for analysing automated acoustic species detection data. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9(3), 560-570.
notes: Counts of classifier detections with false-positive validation.

description: Alder flycatcher removal counts (individuals first detected in each of three 5-minute intervals) at 50 points in Massachusetts beaver meadows, 2005, survey 1, with woody vegetation, structure, time and date covariates (unmarked alfl.csv; Chandler, King & DeStefano 2009). First multinomial_cell table.
reference: Chandler, R. B., King, D. I. & DeStefano, S. (2009). Scrub-shrub bird habitat associations at multiple spatial scales in beaver meadows in Massachusetts. The Auk 126(1), 186-197.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package. occasion indexes the removal interval (standard E9 declared stretch); multinomialType = removal. Round-trip tested in converters/rt_03_alfl_removal.R.

description: Counts of adult common frogs, common toads and alpine newts on four visual-encounter visits at 79 snow-making reservoirs, artificial ponds and natural ponds in the Swiss Alps, summer 2025.
reference: Chanex, A., Schmidt, B. R. & Zemp, C. (2026). The ecological potential of snow-making reservoirs for amphibians in the Swiss Alps. Zenodo data set (Master thesis, University of Neuchatel).
notes: Raw files read from the 1.1 GB zip by range requests.

notes: One table per roost as deposited; POPAN files are a recode of the MS files (not shipped).

description: Annual life-stage histories (multistate: not seen / one linear leaf / one rounded leaf / two-leaved adult / flower spike) of 241 marked Platanthera orbiculata orchids at Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest, 2011-2015, with leaf area per plant-year; source-inferred dormancy and death are y = 0 with the code kept.

description: Daily detection/non-detection (with record counts in y_raw) of 35 bird and mammal taxa at 129 game cameras deployed about a week each at wildlife openings in the Monongahela National Forest, West Virginia, in April-May 2019, 2020 and 2021, with camera-hours per day as effort; one of three datasets behind a deer-coyote two-species occupancy paper.

description: Daily detection/non-detection (with sequence counts in y_raw) of 47 bird and mammal taxa at 146 game cameras deployed about two months each on private land in three West Virginia county pairs in summer 2022, with camera-hours per day as effort, 0.1-degree coordinates and detection distance; one of three datasets behind a deer-coyote two-species occupancy paper.
reference: Clipp, H. L., Pesi, S. M., Miller, M. L., Gigliotti, L. C., Skelly, B. P., & Rota, C. T. (2024). White-tailed deer detection rates increase when coyotes are present. Ecology and Evolution, 14(3), e11149.

reference: Ferguson, P.F.B., Conroy, M.J., & Hepinstall-Cymerman, J. (2015). Occupancy models for data with false positive and false negative errors and heterogeneity across sites and surveys. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 6(12), 1395-1406.
notes: Multi-state response (0/1/2 = none / uncertain / certain detection) for false-positive occupancy models (occuFP type 2). README labels the coordinates UTM but they are decimal degrees. Count protocol details are only in the paper.

description: Daily camera-trap detection/non-detection of coyote, opossum and raccoon at 111 Chicago-area stations over 13 seasons (2010-2013), with urbanisation covariates.
reference: Fidino, M., Simonis, J. L., & Magle, S. B. (2019). A multistate dynamic occupancy model to estimate local colonization-extinction rates and patterns of co-occurrence between two or more interacting species. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 10(2), 233-244.
notes: Dynamic co-occurrence input; overlaps the coyote mange table murray_2021_chicago_coyote_mange (different response).

description: Days seen out of days walked for 193 bird species in Lincoln Park, Chicago, in 16 years across 1898-2015 (three observers, a century apart).
reference: Fidino, M., Bender, J., Limbrick, K., Gallo, T., & Magle, S. B. (2022). Strolling through a century: Replicating historical bird surveys to explore 100 years of change in an urban bird community. The American Naturalist, 199(2).
notes: Historical bird walks; one site.

description: Spatial capture-recapture detections of 23 individually identified Sitka black-tailed deer bucks at 26 camera traps over 32 nights (September-October 2022) on Afognak Island, Alaska, one row per buck x camera x worked night, with camera coordinates in __traps.
reference: Finnegan, S. P., Hinojo, A., Monod, S., Wall, W. A., Olsen, P., & Allen, M. L. (2024). A comparison of thermal drones and camera trap population estimates for Sitka black-tailed deer in Alaska. Wildlife Biology, e01360.
notes: Closed-population SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps. Survey set = deposited camera x night operating matrix. y_raw = independent events (6-min cutoff) per buck-camera-night. Night-to-date mapping read from the captures.

description: Daily detections of Wood Thrush (571 points) and Cerulean Warbler (243 points) over 10 ARU recording days from a human-verified machine-learning classifier, south-western Pennsylvania forests, 2020-2021.
reference: Fiss, C., Lapp, S., Cohen, J., Parker, H., Larkin, J. T., Larkin, J. L., & Kitzes, J. (2024). Performance of unmarked abundance models with data from machine-learning classification of passive acoustic recordings. Ecosphere.
notes: __survey_taxa: Cerulean Warbler classified at two blocks only; paper not read.

description: Two-visit point counts of Wood Thrush and Cerulean Warbler at 573 forest points in south-western Pennsylvania, 2020-2021, with minute of first detection and distance-bin counts.
reference: Fiss, C., Lapp, S., Cohen, J., Parker, H., Larkin, J. T., Larkin, J. L., & Kitzes, J. (2024). Performance of unmarked abundance models with data from machine-learning classification of passive acoustic recordings. Ecosphere.
notes: Distance-bin breaks not deposited; paper not read.

description: Repeated point counts of 32 riparian bird species at 275 points in 23 Great Basin canyons, Nevada, 2001-2018, with canyon riparian covariates.
reference: Fogarty, F. A., Yen, J. D. L., Fleishman, E., Sollmann, R., & Ke, A. (2022). Multiple-region, N-mixture community models to assess associations of riparian area, fragmentation, and species richness. Ecological Applications.
notes: Dynamic community N-mixture; BTAH (undefined code) dropped.

description: Bird point counts at grassland sites managed for northern bobwhite in southern Iowa, three visits a year in 2022-2023, with counts by three-minute interval and distance band of first detection.
notes: Repeated species rows within a visit summed (ruling 2026-11-06), interval x band cells as obs_ columns.

description: Session-level capture histories of 684 introduced feral cats over 196 trapping sessions at three sites on Grande Terre, Kerguelen Islands, 1994-2013, with sex, body condition and session dates.
reference: Fouchet, D., Santin-Janin, H., Sauvage, F., Yoccoz, N. G., & Pontier, D. (2016). An R package for analyzing survival using continuous-time open capture-recapture models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 7.
notes: Dryad version zip; captures pooled to sessions from the deposited session table; age column not shipped.

description: Mist-net detection / non-detection of 42 bat species at 18 forest and farmland sites (6 coffee) in southern Costa Rica, 2009-2013 (185 netting visits, one to three per site per year), with coffee, terrain and tree-cover covariates.
reference: Frank, H. K., Frishkoff, L. O., Mendenhall, C. D., Daily, G. C., & Hadly, E. A. (2017). Phylogeny, traits, and biodiversity of a Neotropical bat assemblage: close relatives show similar responses to local deforestation. The American Naturalist, 190(2), 200-212.
notes: Built from the deposited JAGS input array (array.rdata); visits per site-year (nrep) are the survey set. Site distances and phylogenetic inputs not shipped. Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Camera-trap detection of five large carnivores in 5-day occasions at stations in Zakouma National Park, Chad, dry and wet seasons 2020, with effort and site covariates.
reference: Fraticelli, C., Shams, A., Verschueren, S., Ourde, O., Fekoua, B., Zayed, A. A., Leirs, H., & Bauer, H. (2026). Seasonal dynamics of resource availability and human presence shape habitat use of large carnivores in Chad. Ecology and Evolution, 16.
notes: Dryad version zip; effort table is the survey set; wet-season cheetah and striped hyaena rebuilt from the detection list; prey RAI not shipped.

description: Annual CJS capture histories of 197 eastern hellbenders (Cryptobranchus alleganiensis) in the Hiwassee River, 2004-2008.
notes: Program MARK .inp; no covariates.

description: Detection/non-detection of 74 fish species in 100 HUC12 watersheds of the Upper and Middle New River basin (Virginia/North Carolina) across 25 surveyed three-year primary periods of a 26-period grid (1938-2014; __periods carries all 26), compiled from collection records; years within a period are secondary occasions and the number of collections per HUC-year is the effort covariate.
reference: Frimpong, E. (2017). Fish Detection Histories and Covariates, Upper and Middle New River Drainage Basin (Virginia and North Carolina, USA). Harvard Dataverse, V1.
notes: No associated paper identified on Crossref. Surveyed = at least one collection record that HUC-year.

description: Twelve years (2001-2012) of dry- and wet-season bird surveys on 44 transects in forest, diversified and intensive agriculture across four regions of Costa Rica (Frishkoff et al. 2014, Science): surveys with a detection out of three per transect x season x taxon, 490 taxa (486 species, 4 genus-only records), with land use and region.
reference: Frishkoff, L. O., Karp, D. S., M'Gonigle, L. K., Mendenhall, C. D., Zook, J., Kremen, C., Hadly, E. A., & Daily, G. C. (2014). Loss of avian phylogenetic diversity in neotropical agricultural systems. Science, 345(6202), 1343-1346.
notes: binomial_count (ruling #34): only detections deposited, survey set from row presence per transect-season (8 H-SI wet-season cells absent). Four genus-only records shipped at genus rank; Empidonax traillii (duplicated cells) not shipped. Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Freshwater fish community (50 taxa) detected by MiFish 12S eDNA metabarcoding in three replicate water samples at 50 sites of the Lake Kasumigaura watershed, Japan, August 2017; read counts as y_raw, riverbank vegetation site covariate, primer mismatches per taxon.
reference: Fukaya, K., Kondo, N. I., Matsuzaki, S. S., & Kadoya, T. (2022). Multispecies site occupancy modelling and study design for spatially replicated environmental DNA metabarcoding. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 13(1), 183-193.
notes: Replicate samples as occasions within sites; six samples without reads have no rows. Analysis scripts are a separate MIT Zenodo record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.5515373), not shipped.

description: Daily camera-trap detection/non-detection of 15 carnivores at 1,340 sites in northern California, 2009-2018 (one to three years per site), with fire severity and pyrodiversity covariates; coordinates coarsened.
reference: Furnas, B. J., Goldstein, B. R., & Figura, P. J. (2022). Intermediate fire severity diversity promotes richness of forest carnivores in California. Diversity and Distributions.
notes: Community camera-trap occupancy over 10 years; coordinates coarsened as a precaution (ESA-listed DPSs).

description: Camera-trap detection/non-detection of guigna, Molina's hog-nosed skunk, foxes (Lycalopex), domestic dog and domestic cat at 180 grid-cell camera stations over up to 14 five-night occasions in agricultural landscapes of La Araucania, Chile (2019), with camera nights and human detections per occasion and 13 landscape metrics per station.
reference: Galvez, N., Infante, J., Fernandez, A., Diaz, J., & Petracca, L. (2021). Land use intensification coupled with free-roaming dogs as potential defaunation drivers of mesocarnivores in agricultural landscapes. Journal of Applied Ecology, 58(12), 2962-2974.
notes: Licence conflict: Dryad metadata CC0, deposited readme ODbL/DbCL; the stricter (ODbL) governs and propagates (intake policy). 693 of 2,520 unit-occasions not surveyed (trailing). Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Presence of 123 bird species on 571 point-count visits (property level) to 55 wetland easements in Iowa, 2007-2009 and 2022-2023, with dates, observers, points surveyed, woody cover and easement age.
reference: Gapinski, L.A., Kinkead, K.E., Tucker, A.M., Dinsmore, S.J., and Bishop, T. (2025). Bird point count and covariate data from wetland easements in Iowa, 2007-2009 and 2022-2023 (ver. 3.0). U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Companion tables gapinski_2025_iowawrp_focal_count (counts) and gapinski_2025_iowawrp_point_occ (point level, 2022-2023).

description: Counts (summed over 7-10 points) of 16 conservation-priority bird species on 571 visits to 55 wetland easements in Iowa, 2007-2009 and 2022-2023, with dates, observers and points surveyed.
reference: Gapinski, L.A., Kinkead, K.E., Tucker, A.M., Dinsmore, S.J., and Bishop, T. (2025). Bird point count and covariate data from wetland easements in Iowa, 2007-2009 and 2022-2023 (ver. 3.0). U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Same visits as gapinski_2025_iowawrp_birds_occ; count > 0 exactly where that table has presence (asserted).

description: Presence of 54 bird species at 494 points on 2022-2023 wetland-easement point counts in Iowa (three visits a year), with point vegetation, survey time and observers.
reference: Gapinski, L.A., Kinkead, K.E., Tucker, A.M., Dinsmore, S.J., and Bishop, T. (2025). Bird point count and covariate data from wetland easements in Iowa, 2007-2009 and 2022-2023 (ver. 3.0). U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Point-level analysis set; the property-level tables cover 123 species and 2007-2009 as well.

description: Open-population spatial capture-recapture of tigers at Nagarahole Reserve, India (WCS, 1991-2000): 75 photo-identified individuals x 193 camera stations active in at least one period (195 deposited) x 10 primary periods, y = trap days with a capture per station-period, effort = active trap days; station coordinates centred by the authors (local metres).
reference: Gardner, B., Sollmann, R., Kumar, N. S., Jathanna, D., & Karanth, K. U. (2018). State space and movement specification in open population spatial capture-recapture models. Ecology and Evolution, 8(20), 10336-10344.
notes: First open-population SCR table (E9 experimental). Station-period level (count + effort), no occasion: per-day effort not deposited. Coordinates centred by the source.

description: Camera-trap days-with-detection out of days operated for 38 mammal species at 60 stations in Gorongosa National Park, Mozambique, with site covariates and functional groups.
reference: Gaynor, K. M., Daskin, J. H., Rich, L. N., & Brashares, J. S. (2021). Postwar wildlife recovery in an African savanna: Evaluating patterns and drivers of species occupancy and richness. Animal Conservation, 24(3).
notes: binomial_count (ruling #34).

description: Annual multistate encounter histories (pre-breeder / breeder / non-breeder) of 2,734 known-age echo parakeets ringed as nestlings in Mauritius (1994-2021 cohorts), one state per breeding season 1994-2022; rows from the ringing season.
reference: Gellé, A., et al. (2026). Demographic responses to population recovery illustrated by 30 years of monitoring a once critically endangered parrot. Journal of Applied Ecology, 63.
notes: Authors' analysis set (known-age wild birds only). Species IUCN VU; no coordinates in the deposit.

description: Calling index (0-3) of 14 anuran species inside the survey area, with the index outside it, on 1,779 night-time surveys at 52 sites in Big Thicket National Preserve, Texas, 2010-2018.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H. (2020). Data from visual encounter and acoustic monitoring surveys targeting amphibians and reptiles in Big Thicket National Preserve in southeast Texas from August 2010 to September 2018. U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Ordinal calling index; __survey_taxa omits E. cystignathoides where it was not scored. Companion table glorioso_2020_bigthicket_ves.

description: Counts of 37 amphibian and reptile species on 1,779 night-time visual encounter surveys at 52 sites in Big Thicket National Preserve, Texas, 2010-2018, with duration, weather, water temperature and salinity, observers and site coordinates.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H. (2020). Data from visual encounter and acoustic monitoring surveys targeting amphibians and reptiles in Big Thicket National Preserve in southeast Texas from August 2010 to September 2018. U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: ARMI protocol as in glorioso_2025_atchafalaya_ves; companion table glorioso_2020_bigthicket_calls.

description: Counts of seven turtle species, including the alligator snapping turtle, caught in baited hoop nets on two consecutive nightly checks at each of 119 trap sites in south-central Louisiana, 2019, with trap-site habitat, net and bait.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H. (2021). Data from a 2019 occupancy survey of alligator snapping turtles, Macrochelys temminckii, in south-central Louisiana. U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Catch strings parsed to species counts; locations to parish only, as published.

description: Calling index (0 none to 3 full chorus) of 14 frog and toad species inside the study plot on 2,216 night-time site visits at 70 Atchafalaya Basin sites, Louisiana (2008-2016), with the outside-plot index as a covariate, survey conditions, observers and site coordinates.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H., 2025, Data from time-constrained visual encounter surveys and acoustic surveys for amphibians and reptiles in the Atchafalaya Basin conducted from 2008 through 2016: U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Ordinal calling index (responseType ordinal, standard E2). Orphan Sample ID 348 and five 'done in error' samples dropped. Companion: glorioso_2025_atchafalaya_ves.

description: Counts of 47 amphibian and reptile species on 2,216 night-time time-constrained visual encounter surveys at 70 sites in the Atchafalaya Basin, Louisiana (2008-2016; 4-6 samples per site-year), with survey duration, weather and water variables, observers, and site coordinates.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H., 2025, Data from time-constrained visual encounter surveys and acoustic surveys for amphibians and reptiles in the Atchafalaya Basin conducted from 2008 through 2016: U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Zeros built from the sample table (a sample exists iff a row in Sample_Data). Orphan Sample ID 348 and five 'done in error' samples dropped. Companion table: glorioso_2025_atchafalaya_calls.

reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H. (2026). Data from a capture-mark-recapture survey of native treefrogs in Bayou Teche National Wildlife Refuge, Louisiana from 2017 to 2023. U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: CJS per species; companion of glorioso_2026_bayouteche_pipe_count (same surveys).

notes: CJS per species; companion of glorioso_2026_bayouteche_pipe_count (same surveys).

reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H. (2026). Data from a capture-mark-recapture survey of native treefrogs in Bayou Teche National Wildlife Refuge, Louisiana from 2017 to 2023. U.S. Geological Survey data release.

notes: CJS per species; companion of glorioso_2026_bayouteche_pipe_count (same surveys).

notes: unit = pipe, period = study month; the tagged-frog histories are not built.

reference: Goldberg, J. F., Tempa, T., Norbu, N., Hebblewhite, M., Mills, L. S., Wangchuk, T. R., & Lukacs, P. (2015). Examining temporal sample scale and model choice with spatial capture-recapture models in the common leopard Panthera pardus. PLOS ONE, 10(11), e0140757.
notes: Closed SCR; survey set from the paper's statement of continuous operation (inferred); traps centred (IUCN VU).

description: Weekly camera detections of mammals and the lace monitor in road underpasses and forest, Port Macquarie, NSW, 2013-2017.

notes: Road underpass use; weekly detections.

description: Detection of brush-tailed phascogale and inland sugar glider in nest boxes at 74 box clusters, Diamond Hill, Bendigo Regional Park, Victoria, Australia, at 12 twice-yearly censuses from May 2018 to October 2023.
reference: Goldingay, R., Thomas, K. & Quin, D. (2026). Can artificial tree cavities provide population support to cavity-dependent non-flying mammals? Ecology and Evolution. https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.74280
notes: Cluster-level detection per census; female-phascogale file and camera study not shipped.

description: American pika (Ochotona princeps) sign surveys at 771 plots in five national park units of Oregon, Idaho and California, 2010-2014 and 2017-2021, with partial within-year resurveys and per-survey counts of each sign type (old and fresh scat and haypiles, calls, sightings).
reference: Goldman, M. R., Shinderman, M., Jeffress, M. R., Rodhouse, T. J., & Shoemaker, K. T. (2023). Integrating multiple sign types to improve occupancy estimation for inconspicuous species. Ecology and Evolution, 13(5), e10019.

notes: Dynamic occupancy with sign-type counts as obs_ columns (multi-sign model refittable); y = any fresh sign, as in the paper (old sign in obs_ columns).

description: Weekly ARU detection/non-detection of ruffed grouse drumming at 299 managed-forest points in Pennsylvania, 2021-2023, five weeks per point, with recording minutes, stand and landscape covariates.
reference: Goldman, J. et al. (2025). Does a decision support tool designed to depict West Nile Virus risk explain variation in ruffed grouse (Bonasa umbellus) use of managed forests? Wildlife Biology.
notes: Acoustic single-season occupancy; zero-minute weeks dropped as not surveyed.

description: Counts of wood frog and spotted salamander egg masses and larvae by each of two observers on 1,714 visits to 108 vernal pools at Canaan Valley National Wildlife Refuge, West Virginia, 2004-2016, with harvest treatment, pool dryness, water chemistry and pool size.
reference: Grant, E.H.C., and Brand, A.B. (2023). Long-term effects of timber harvest on vernal pool availability and occupancy of two obligate amphibians. U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: taxon = species x stage (egg masses, larvae); occasion = visit x observer slot.

description: Hair-snare genetic SCR of 138 fishers at 100 northwestern California sites, 2006-2013 (snare-year binomial counts).
reference: Green, D. S. et al. (2018). Dynamic occupancy modeling reveals a hierarchy of competition among fishers, grey foxes, and ringtails. Journal of Animal Ecology, 87(3), 813-824.
notes: SCR (E9 experimental), binomial per snare-year.

description: Track-plate detections of fisher, grey fox and ringtail at 100 sites in northwestern California, autumn 2007-2013.
reference: Green, D. S. et al. (2018). Dynamic occupancy modeling reveals a hierarchy of competition among fishers, grey foxes, and ringtails. Journal of Animal Ecology, 87(3), 813-824.
notes: Dynamic co-occurrence of three mesocarnivores.

reference: Hamer, A. J. et al. (2016). Manipulating wetland hydroperiod to improve occupancy rates by an endangered amphibian: modelling management scenarios. Journal of Applied Ecology.

reference: Raman, T. R. S. (2006). Effects of habitat structure and adjacent habitats on birds in tropical rainforest fragments and shaded plantations in the Western Ghats, India. Biodiversity and Conservation 15, 1577-1607. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10531-005-2352-5
notes: E7.3 sibling of raman_2006_anamalai_birds_count without Buceros bicornis and Ocyceros griseus (VU).

'sp.' and slash records at their lowest common rank.
